subject: call to inla crashes every time

messages.author: 10a9a7970eb46cba
messages.subject: call to inla crashes every time
parts:
Hi all,

I am completely new to the INLA package and have yet to successfully create a model. We are using it for avian habitat selection models. One second after calling inla, I always get a fatal error detailed below. It doesn't seem to be related to the data, though I can share that if you suspect I'm wrong. 

Call:
ord3.inla  <- inla(formula.ord3.inla, family ="binomial", data=ord3_rsfha, weights=ord3_rsfha$weight,
                   control.fixed = list(
                     mean = 0,
                     prec = list(hab = prec.beta.hab)
                   ),
                   control.compute=list(return.marginals.predictor=TRUE), verbose = TRUE
)

Stop message
readlink: illegal option -- f
usage: readlink [-n] [file ...]
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac.arm64/inla.run: line 65: ./: is a directory
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac.arm64/inla.run: line 71: /Volumes/Buddy SSD 1/West_Ch2_Models/Habitat Selection Files/: is a directory
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac.arm64/inla.run: line 71: exec: /Volumes/Buddy SSD 1/West_Ch2_Models/Habitat Selection Files/: cannot execute: Undefined error: 0
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

Based on this output, what might be going on? I am running R 4.3 on a MacOS Monterey. I installed the INLA package directly from GitHub, and I have tried re-installing. Thank you so much in advance for any help. 

Best,

Miles Buddy
North Carolina State University
